hooks.text: A 12-mile-high mountain ridge wraps around Saturn's moon Iapetus.
Saturn's moon Iapetus is shaped like a giant walnut.
A 12-mile-high ridge encircles three-quarters of a moon.

title: The Saturn Moon Shaped Like a Walnut
description: Saturn's moon Iapetus features a 12-mile-high wall along its equator and a surface split between jet-black dust and bright water ice.

beats.text: A 12-mile-high mountain ridge wraps around Saturn's moon Iapetus.
beats.visual: Cassini spacecraft image showing the equatorial ridge of Iapetus, 2004

beats.text: It turns the third-largest moon of Saturn into a giant walnut.
beats.visual: Cassini global mosaic of Saturn moon Iapetus showing walnut shape, 2007

beats.text: Peaks along this equatorial wall rise 12 miles above the plains.
beats.visual: Close-up Cassini photograph of high mountain peaks on Iapetus, 2007

beats.text: On one side, dark material forms a layer only one foot thick.
beats.visual: Cassini Regio dark terrain close-up showing impact craters on Iapetus, 2007

beats.text: That side is ten times darker, reflecting just three percent of light.
beats.visual: Transition zone between black and bright surface terrain on Iapetus, 2007
queries: Iapetus crater dark and bright slopes

beats.text: The other side shines ten times brighter, covered in pure ice.
beats.visual: Bright ice-covered hemisphere of Iapetus imaged by Cassini, 2007

beats.text: Sunlight boils ice from the dark side onto the bright side.
beats.visual: Cassini view of bright crater rims and dark crater floors on Iapetus, 2007
queries: Iapetus crater dark and bright slopes

beats.text: Yet this bizarre world still keeps its 12-mile-high equatorial ridge.
beats.visual: Cassini global view of two-toned moon Iapetus with visible equatorial ridge, 2004

better_than_last: Applies scale_ladder by stepping up from the 12-mile peak height to the paper-thin surface coating, extreme brightness contrast, and runaway ice sublimation mechanics.
